name: After the Four
sub: 41 AH to the fall of Baghdad, 661 to 1258 CE

events.title: Hasan hands over: the Year of Unity
events.summary: After Ali's death the people of Kufa pledge to his son Hasan. After some months he gives the caliphate to Mu'awiyah to end the bloodshed, and the year is called the Year of the Community.

refs.checked: sunnah.com numbering, read on the hadith-api copy

steps.title: Hasan is pledged
steps.summary: The people of Kufa pledge to Hasan, the Prophet's grandson, who rules for about six months.

steps.title: The agreement
steps.when: Rabi al-Awwal to Jumada al-Ula 41 AH
steps.summary: Both armies face each other, and Hasan gives the matter to Mu'awiyah on terms, to spare Muslim blood. Reports differ on the terms.

steps.title: The Prophet's saying
steps.summary: The Prophet had called Hasan a leader and said Allah would make peace between two large groups of Muslims through him. The scholars of hadith note this as it came true.

refs.checked: sunnah.com numbering, read on the hadith-api copy

steps.title: The Year of the Community
steps.summary: The people gather under one caliph, and the year is named the Year of the Community.

events.title: Mu'awiyah and the Umayyad caliphate in Damascus
events.summary: Mu'awiyah ibn Abi Sufyan, governor of Sham for about twenty years, is now caliph from Damascus. His reign lasts about nineteen to twenty years and passes to his son Yazid.

steps.title: Damascus as the seat
steps.summary: The capital moves from Madinah and Kufa to Damascus; Mu'awiyah governs Iraq through governors such as al-Mughirah and Ziyad ibn Abihi.

steps.title: Fleet and frontiers
steps.summary: He maintains a navy, sends repeated campaigns toward Constantinople, and continues the push into North Africa, where Uqbah ibn Nafi founds Qayrawan in 50 AH.

steps.title: Yazid named heir
steps.summary: Mu'awiyah has the oath taken for his son Yazid, the first time a caliph's son is named in his lifetime; some leading figures object. Scholars judge the step differently.

steps.title: Mu'awiyah's death
steps.summary: He dies in Damascus in Rajab 60 AH, in old age, and Yazid succeeds.

events.title: Karbala and the martyrdom of Husayn
events.summary: Husayn ibn Ali, the Prophet's grandson, leaves Makkah after letters from Kufa and is killed with many of his family at Karbala on 10 Muharram 61 AH.

steps.title: Husayn will not pledge to Yazid
steps.summary: After Mu'awiyah's death Husayn declines to pledge to Yazid and leaves Madinah for Makkah. Ibn Abbas and others advise him not to go to Iraq.

steps.title: Letters from Kufa
steps.summary: Kufans write inviting him; his cousin Muslim ibn Aqil is sent ahead and is killed in Kufa by the governor Ubaydullah ibn Ziyad, and the support melts away.

steps.title: The day of Ashura
steps.summary: Husayn's small party is met by an army of the governor at Karbala; after refusing to give way he is killed with most of the men of his household.

steps.title: Aftermath
steps.summary: The survivors are taken to Damascus and then sent home to Madinah. Sources agree on the main events but differ on details and on where his head was kept.

events.title: The second fitnah and Ibn al-Zubayr
events.summary: Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr refuses to pledge to Yazid and is acknowledged as caliph in Hijaz and much of the empire. Abd al-Malik ends the split in 73 AH.

steps.title: The people of Madinah and al-Harra
steps.summary: Madinah rejects Yazid, and a Syrian army defeats its people at al-Harra. Many companions' children are killed, and the city is plundered.

steps.title: The siege of Makkah
steps.summary: The Syrian army besieges Makkah, the Ka'bah is damaged, and Yazid's death stops the siege. Ibn al-Zubayr later rebuilds the Ka'bah.

steps.title: Rival claims
steps.summary: Ibn al-Zubayr is accepted in Hijaz, Iraq and Egypt for a time; Marwan ibn al-Hakam, then Abd al-Malik, hold Syria.

steps.title: The end
steps.summary: Al-Hajjaj ibn Yusuf besieges Makkah; Ibn al-Zubayr is killed fighting, and the empire is again under one ruler.

events.title: Abd al-Malik, Arabic coinage and the Dome of the Rock
events.summary: Abd al-Malik builds the Dome of the Rock, whose inscription is dated 72 AH, and makes Arabic the language of the registers and coin.

steps.title: The Dome of the Rock
steps.summary: The building's inscription gives 72 AH. Its purpose is debated: honouring the rock of the Night Journey, a rival to Byzantine churches, or a sign of the new state.

steps.title: Arabic coinage
steps.summary: Coins with Arabic Islamic inscriptions replace Byzantine and Persian types, minted in the name of the caliph's government. Some scholars date the first full reform to 77 AH.

steps.title: The registers in Arabic
steps.summary: The diwans of Iraq and Sham move from Persian and Greek into Arabic.

events.title: The conquest of Spain and Sindh
events.summary: At either end of the empire, Tariq ibn Ziyad crosses to Spain in 92 AH and Muhammad ibn al-Qasim reaches Sindh in 93 AH.

steps.title: Tariq crosses
steps.summary: Tariq ibn Ziyad, a lieutenant of Musa ibn Nusayr, lands near the rock later called Jabal Tariq with a small force.

steps.title: Defeat of Roderic
steps.summary: He defeats the Visigothic king Roderic near the river Guadalete. Toledo and Cordoba are taken in the following months, and Musa follows in 93 AH.

steps.title: Sindh
steps.summary: Muhammad ibn al-Qasim takes Debal and later Aror and Multan. Sources differ on the order and the exact years.

events.title: Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz
events.summary: A short reign of about two and a half years that later scholars remember for justice, fair taxes and care for the Sunnah; some call him the fifth of the rightly-guided.

steps.title: Accession
steps.summary: He is named by Sulayman ibn Abd al-Malik, accepts reluctantly, and gives up the luxury of his household.

steps.title: Justice and the treasury
steps.summary: He returns property taken unjustly, relieves converts of the poll tax in practice, and lowers burdens on the provinces.

steps.title: Writing down the Sunnah
steps.summary: He writes to governors and scholars, including Abu Bakr ibn Hazm, to record the hadith before its carriers are lost.

steps.title: His death
steps.summary: He dies at Dayr Sim'an in Syria in Rajab 101 AH, at about forty; some reports say he was poisoned, and this is not settled.

events.title: The Abbasid revolution
events.summary: A movement from Khurasan under Abu Muslim brings down the Umayyads. Abu al-Abbas al-Saffah is pledged as caliph in Kufa, and Marwan II is defeated at the Zab.

steps.title: The rising in Khurasan
steps.summary: Abu Muslim al-Khurasani raises the black banners in Marw in the name of the Prophet's family and wins the east.

steps.title: Al-Saffah pledged
steps.summary: Abu al-Abbas, a descendant of the Prophet's uncle al-Abbas, is pledged in Kufa and gives his first speech in the mosque.

steps.title: The Greater Zab
steps.summary: The last Umayyad caliph Marwan ibn Muhammad is beaten near the Zab river, flees through Syria to Egypt, and is killed there in Dhu al-Hijjah 132 AH.

steps.title: A survivor in the west
steps.summary: Abd al-Rahman ibn Muawiyah escapes the purge and founds an Umayyad emirate in Cordoba in 138 AH.

events.title: Baghdad founded
events.summary: Al-Mansur builds the Round City on the Tigris as the Abbasid capital. In the following century it becomes a centre of translation and learning, and four imams live there or nearby.

steps.title: The Round City
steps.summary: Al-Mansur chooses the site on the Tigris and lays out a round walled city with the palace and mosque at its centre.

steps.title: The age of translation
steps.summary: Under Harun al-Rashid and al-Ma'mun, Greek, Persian and Indian works are translated into Arabic with state support. The scale of the Bayt al-Hikmah is debated among historians.

steps.title: The four imams
steps.summary: Abu Hanifah (died 150), Malik ibn Anas (died 179), al-Shafi'i (died 204) and Ahmad ibn Hanbal (died 241) lived across this period; al-Shafi'i and Ahmad taught in Baghdad.

events.title: The Mihnah and Ahmad ibn Hanbal
events.summary: Al-Ma'mun orders scholars to affirm that the Qur'an is created. Ahmad ibn Hanbal refuses, is imprisoned and flogged, and his steadfastness is widely remembered.

steps.title: The order
steps.summary: Al-Ma'mun, shortly before his death, writes to his governor in Baghdad to test judges and scholars on the createdness of the Qur'an.

steps.title: Ahmad refuses
steps.summary: Ahmad ibn Hanbal and a few others refuse; he is taken in chains toward Tarsus, and returned to Baghdad after Ma'mun's death.

steps.title: The flogging
steps.summary: Under al-Mu'tasim he is flogged and held for months, and does not change his words.

steps.title: The end of the Mihnah
steps.summary: Al-Mutawakkil ends the test, and Ahmad's position becomes the standard one; he dies in 241 AH.

events.title: The Mongol sack of Baghdad
events.summary: Hulagu's Mongol army besieges Baghdad, takes it in Safar 656 AH, and ends the Abbasid caliphate there.

steps.title: The siege
steps.summary: Hulagu's army surrounds the city and shells the walls; the caliph al-Musta'sim negotiates and fails.

steps.title: The fall and the sack
steps.summary: The city surrenders after about two weeks and is plundered for about a week; sources give death tolls from tens of thousands to a million, and none is reliable.

steps.title: The caliph killed
steps.summary: Al-Musta'sim is put to death, ending the Abbasid caliphate in Baghdad.
